claim: Microtubules are dynamic polymers consisting of αβ-tubulin heterodimers.
source: Microtubules are dynamic polymers consisting of αβ-tubulin heterodimers.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology presented in the abstract.

claim: The initial polymerization process, called microtubule nucleation, occurs spontaneously via αβ-tubulin.
source: The initial polymerization process, called microtubule nucleation, occurs spontaneously via αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: A large energy barrier prevents microtubule nucleation in cells.
source: Since a large energy barrier prevents microtubule nucleation in cells, the γ-tubulin ring complex is recruited to the centrosome to overcome the nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is established knowledge about microtubule nucleation barriers.

claim: The γ-tubulin ring complex is recruited to the centrosome to overcome the nucleation barrier.
source: Since a large energy barrier prevents microtubule nucleation in cells, the γ-tubulin ring complex is recruited to the centrosome to overcome the nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is established knowledge about centrosomal microtubule nucleation.

claim: A considerable number of microtubules can polymerize independently of the centrosome in various cell types.
source: However, a considerable number of microtubules can polymerize independently of the centrosome in various cell types.
evidence: This is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: CAMSAP2 serves as a strong nucleator for microtubule formation by significantly reducing the nucleation barrier.
source: Here, we present evidence that the minus-end-binding calmodulin-regulated spectrin-associated protein 2 (CAMSAP2) serves as a strong nucleator for microtubule formation by significantly reducing the nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: CAMSAP2 co-condensates with αβ-tubulin via a phase separation process.
source: CAMSAP2 co-condensates with αβ-tubulin via a phase separation process, producing plenty of nucleation intermediates.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: CAMSAP2-tubulin co-condensates produce plenty of nucleation intermediates.
source: CAMSAP2 co-condensates with αβ-tubulin via a phase separation process, producing plenty of nucleation intermediates.
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Microtubules radiate from the CAMSAP2-tubulin co-condensates, resulting in aster-like structure formation.
source: Microtubules then radiate from the co-condensates, resulting in aster-like structure formation.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy and EM data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: CAMSAP2 localizes at the co-condensates.
source: CAMSAP2 localizes at the co-condensates and decorates the radiating microtubule lattices to some extent.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 4.

claim: CAMSAP2 decorates the radiating microtubule lattices to some extent.
source: CAMSAP2 localizes at the co-condensates and decorates the radiating microtubule lattices to some extent.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 1D and Figure 4.

claim: CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by organizing a nucleation centre.
source: Taken together, these in vitro findings suggest that CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by organizing a nucleation centre as well as by stabilizing microtubule intermediates and growing microtubules.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by stabilizing microtubule intermediates.
source: Taken together, these in vitro findings suggest that CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by organizing a nucleation centre as well as by stabilizing microtubule intermediates and growing microtubules.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data, particularly the EM observations of intermediates.

claim: CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by stabilizing growing microtubules.
source: Taken together, these in vitro findings suggest that CAMSAP2 supports microtubule nucleation and growth by organizing a nucleation centre as well as by stabilizing microtubule intermediates and growing microtubules.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing CAMSAP2 decoration of microtubules.

claim: Microtubules contribute to fundamental processes in cells, such as cell shape determination, chromosome segregation, cilium and flagellum formation, and molecular motor trafficking.
source: Microtubules are dynamic tubular polymers that contribute to fundamental processes in cells, such as cell shape determination, chromosome segregation, cilium and flagellum formation, and molecular motor trafficking (Desai and Mitchison, 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: α-tubulin and β-tubulin align head-to-tail to form protofilaments that associate laterally to grow into microtubules.
source: α-tubulin and β-tubulin align head-to-tail to form protofilaments that associate laterally grow into the microtubules (Alushin et al., 2014; Nogales et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The exposed β-tubulin end is called the plus-end.
source: The exposed β-tubulin end is called the plus-end, whereas the exposed α-tubulin end is called the minus-end.
evidence: This is standard nomenclature in the field.

claim: The exposed α-tubulin end is called the minus-end.
source: The exposed β-tubulin end is called the plus-end, whereas the exposed α-tubulin end is called the minus-end.
evidence: This is standard nomenclature in the field.

claim: The microtubule plus-end is more dynamic than the minus-end.
source: The microtubule plus-end is more dynamic than the minus-end; it dynamically alternates between growth and shrinkage.
evidence: This is established knowledge about microtubule dynamics.

claim: The microtubule plus-end dynamically alternates between growth and shrinkage.
source: The microtubule plus-end is more dynamic than the minus-end; it dynamically alternates between growth and shrinkage.
evidence: This is established knowledge about microtubule dynamics.

claim: The dynamic events of microtubule plus-ends are regulated by many microtubule plus-end-tracking proteins (+TIPs).
source: The dynamic events are regulated by many microtubule plus-end-tracking proteins (+TIPs) (Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2015; Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2008; Howard and Hyman, 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The minus-end is less dynamic than the plus-end.
source: The minus-end is less dynamic and is responsible for determining the geometry of microtubule networks by stably anchoring at microtubule nucleation sites or the microtubule organizing centre (Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2019; Dammermann et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The minus-end is responsible for determining the geometry of microtubule networks by stably anchoring at microtubule nucleation sites or the microtubule organizing centre.
source: The minus-end is less dynamic and is responsible for determining the geometry of microtubule networks by stably anchoring at microtubule nucleation sites or the microtubule organizing centre (Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2019; Dammermann et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Only a few minus-end-binding proteins (−TIPs) have been reported, including γ-tubulin and calmodulin-regulated spectrin-associated proteins (CAMSAPs).
source: Despite the identification of many +TIPs, only a few minus-end-binding proteins (−TIPs) have been reported, including γ-tubulin and calmodulin-regulated spectrin-associated proteins (CAMSAPs).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: γ-Tubulin forms a ring complex (γ-TuRC) that is located at centrosomes to nucleate microtubules and stabilize the microtubule minus-ends.
source: γ-Tubulin which forms a ring complex (γ-TuRC) is located at centrosomes to nucleate microtubules and stabilize the microtubule minus-ends (Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: γ-TuRC serves as a nucleation template for centrosomal microtubule formation by aligning αβ-tubulins to form the tubular structure of the microtubule in a process called templated nucleation.
source: γ-TuRC serves as a nucleation template for centrosomal microtubule formation by aligning αβ-tubulins to form the tubular structure of the microtubule in a process called templated nucleation (Moritz et al., 1995; Roostalu and Surrey, 2017; Wieczorek et al., 2020; Zheng et al., 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The CAMSAP protein family is composed of CAMSAP1-3 in vertebrates, Patronin in Drosophila melanogaster, and PTRN-1 in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: CAMSAPs, the protein family composed of CAMSAP1-3 in vertebrates, Patronin in Drosophila melanogaster, and PaTRoNin (microtubule-binding protein) homolog (PTRN-1) in Caenorhabditis elegans, have been reported to be involved in non-centrosomal microtubule formation (Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Marcette et al., 2014; Meng et al., 2008; Richardson et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CAMSAPs have been reported to be involved in non-centrosomal microtubule formation.
source: CAMSAPs, the protein family composed of CAMSAP1-3 in vertebrates, Patronin in Drosophila melanogaster, and PaTRoNin (microtubule-binding protein) homolog (PTRN-1) in Caenorhabditis elegans, have been reported to be involved in non-centrosomal microtubule formation (Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Marcette et al., 2014; Meng et al., 2008; Richardson et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CAMSAPs generally bind to the growing microtubule minus-ends and strongly suppress the dynamicity of non-centrosomal microtubules in different cell types.
source: Although several in vitro reconstitution experiments have shown differences among CAMSAPs, CAMSAPs generally bind to the growing microtubule minus-ends and strongly suppress the dynamicity of non-centrosomal microtubules in different cell types, including neurons and epithelial cells (Chuang et al., 2014; Hannak et al., 2002; Jiang et al., 2014; Martin et al., 2018; Nashchekin et al., 2016; Noordstra et al., 2016; Pongrakhananon et al., 2018; Sampaio et al., 2001; Tanaka et al., 2012; Toya et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016; Yau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The minus-end side of the microtubule lattice, but not the very end, is recognized by the CKK domain.
source: The minus-end side of the microtubule lattice, but not the very end, is recognized by the CKK domain, although some additional effects were detected by other regions of CAMSAPs (Atherton et al., 2019; Atherton et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CAMSAPs have been reported to act in parallel with γ-TuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation.
source: CAMSAPs have been reported to act in parallel with γ-TuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation, and the microtubule-severing protein katanin regulates the functions of the CAMSAPs (Jiang et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The microtubule-severing protein katanin regulates the functions of the CAMSAPs.
source: CAMSAPs have been reported to act in parallel with γ-TuRC-dependent microtubule nucleation, and the microtubule-severing protein katanin regulates the functions of the CAMSAPs (Jiang et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CAMSAPs are rapidly recruited to and decorate pre-existing nascent microtubule minus-ends to sustain non-centrosomal microtubules.
source: CAMSAPs are rapidly recruited to and to decorate pre-existing nascent microtubule minus-ends to sustain non-centrosomal microtubules.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Some reports have demonstrated the possibility that CAMSAP-containing foci are involved in promoting microtubule nucleation independently of γ-TuRC.
source: On the other hand, some reports have demonstrated the possibility that CAMSAP-containing foci are involved in promoting microtubule nucleation independently of γ-TuRC (Atherton et al., 2019; Jiang et al., 2018; Nashchekin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The mechanism by which CAMSAP2 proteins contribute to non-centrosomal microtubule organization has remained controversial.
source: Thus, the mechanism by which CAMSAP2 proteins contribute to non-centrosomal microtubule organization has remained controversial.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Recent studies suggest that microtubules in cells often nucleate independently of the γ-TuRC template.
source: Recent studies suggest that microtubules in cells often nucleate independently of the γ-TuRC template (Hannak et al., 2002; O'Toole et al., 2012; Sampaio et al., 2001; Tsuchiya and Goshima, 2021; Yau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Full-length CAMSAP2 constructs with and without GFP-tag were purified to show a single peak in size exclusion chromatography.
source: As shown in Figure 1B and C, full-length CAMSAP2 constructs with (GFP-CAMSAP2-FL) and without GFP-tag (CAMSAP2-FL) were purified to show a single peak in size exclusion chromatography.
evidence: This is supported by the chromatography data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL was eluted slightly earlier than the non-tagged construct due to the size of the GFP-tag.
source: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL was eluted slightly earlier than the non-tagged construct due to the size of the GFP-tag, indicating that both constructs should be in the same oligomeric state.
evidence: This is an inference from the chromatography data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Both CAMSAP2-FL and GFP-CAMSAP2-FL constructs are in the same oligomeric state.
source: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL was eluted slightly earlier than the non-tagged construct due to the size of the GFP-tag, indicating that both constructs should be in the same oligomeric state.
evidence: This is an inference from the chromatography data.

claim: The molecular mass of CAMSAP2-FL was examined by multi-angle light scattering (MALS) as 122 ± 1.1 kDa.
source: The molecular mass of CAMSAP2-FL was further examined by multi-angle light scattering (MALS) as 122 ± 1.1 kDa (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by MALS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CAMSAP2-FL likely exists as a monomer in solution.
source: Considering that the estimated molecular weight of CAMSAP2-FL is 167 kDa, it likely exists as a monomer in the solution.
evidence: This is an inference from the MALS data showing 122 kDa compared to the theoretical 167 kDa.

claim: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL bound to the microtubule lattice preferentially via the minus-ends.
source: The results showed that GFP-CAMSAP2-FL bound to the microtubule lattice preferentially via the minus-ends, consistent with previous reports (Atherton et al., 2017; Jiang et al., 2014; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 1D and is consistent with previous reports.

claim: The CAMSAP2 proteins used in this study retained their original ability to bind to the microtubule minus-ends.
source: These observations collectively indicate that the CAMSAP2 proteins used in this study retained their original ability to bind to the microtubule minus-ends.
evidence: This is an inference from the binding data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Microtubule nucleation from αβ-tubulin heterodimers can occur spontaneously in vitro.
source: Microtubule nucleation from αβ-tubulin heterodimers (hereafter called tubulin in the Results section) can occur spontaneously in vitro (Kuchnir and Leibler, 1995; Voter and Erickson, 1984).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: De novo microtubule nucleation in vitro requires a critical tubulin concentration greater than 20 µM (CcMT nucleation).
source: De novo microtubule nucleation in vitro requires a critical tubulin concentration greater than 20 µM (CcMT nucleation) (Wieczorek et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The critical concentration for microtubule polymerization (CcMT polymerization) from seeds is typically approximately 1–2 µM.
source: This concentration is considerably higher than that required for microtubule elongation from seeds, which is typically approximately 1–2 µM and is called the critical concentration for microtubule polymerization (CcMT polymerization).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: De novo nucleation of microtubules (CcMT nucleation) was detected just above the tubulin concentration of 20 µM.
source: We detected de novo nucleation of microtubules (CcMT nucleation) just above the tubulin concentration of 20 µM, which is consistent with a previous report and our result by pelleting assay without modification (Wieczorek et al., 2015; Figure 2A and C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data shown in Figure 2A and C.

claim: Tubulin can be pelleted from 1.0 to 2.0 µM in the presence of 1.0 µM CAMSAP2-FL.
source: We found that tubulin can be pelleted from 1.0 to 2.0 µM in the presence of 1.0 µM CAMSAP2-FL, indicating that tubulins could polymerize into microtubules or tubulin oligomers at a close concentration to the CcMT polymerization with CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Tubulins could polymerize into microtubules or tubulin oligomers at a concentration close to the CcMT polymerization with CAMSAP2-FL.
source: We found that tubulin can be pelleted from 1.0 to 2.0 µM in the presence of 1.0 µM CAMSAP2-FL, indicating that tubulins could polymerize into microtubules or tubulin oligomers at a close concentration to the CcMT polymerization with CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is an inference from the pelleting assay data.

claim: CAMSAP2 drastically reduced the nucleation barrier to a level close to the theoretical limit of microtubule polymerization.
source: CAMSAP2 drastically reduced the nucleation barrier to a level close to the theoretical limit of microtubule polymerization.
evidence: This is an inference from the pelleting assay data showing polymerization at 1-2 µM tubulin with CAMSAP2.

claim: Both tubulin and CAMSAP2-FL in the pellet were recovered from the supernatant after incubation on ice.
source: In this assay, both tubulin and CAMSAP2-FL in the pellet were recovered from the supernatant after incubation on ice, suggesting that CAMSAP2-FL co-precipitated with tubulins and this precipitation is reversible.
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data.

claim: CAMSAP2-FL co-precipitated with tubulins and this precipitation is reversible.
source: In this assay, both tubulin and CAMSAP2-FL in the pellet were recovered from the supernatant after incubation on ice, suggesting that CAMSAP2-FL co-precipitated with tubulins and this precipitation is reversible.
evidence: This is an inference from the pelleting assay data.

claim: Polymerization was detected from 250 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM.
source: Polymerization was detected from 250 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM, and 500 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM +100 mM KCl, albeit the polymerization efficiency considerably decreased by increasing the salt concentration (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Polymerization was detected from 500 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM +100 mM KCl.
source: Polymerization was detected from 250 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM, and 500 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM +100 mM KCl, albeit the polymerization efficiency considerably decreased by increasing the salt concentration (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The polymerization efficiency considerably decreased by increasing the salt concentration.
source: Polymerization was detected from 250 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM, and 500 nM CAMSAP2-FL in PEM +100 mM KCl, albeit the polymerization efficiency considerably decreased by increasing the salt concentration (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by the pelleting assay data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: CAMSAP2 significantly enhances the nucleation and polymerization of tubulin.
source: These results suggest that CAMSAP2 significantly enhances the nucleation and polymerization of tubulin.
evidence: This is an inference from the pelleting assay data.

claim: The enhancement effect of CAMSAP2 on tubulin polymerization still exists in the physiological condition, although it became milder than in the tubulin polymerization buffer.
source: The enhancement effect still exists in the physiological condition, although it became milder than the tubulin polymerization buffer.
evidence: This is an inference from the pelleting assay data comparing PEM and PEM+KCl conditions.

claim: CAMSAP2 possesses a long disordered region at the middle portion.
source: CAMSAP2 also possesses a long disordered region at the middle portion, as predicted by program PONDR, indicating its potential for phase separation (Figure 3A; Romero et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by the PONDR prediction shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CAMSAP2 has potential for phase separation.
source: CAMSAP2 also possesses a long disordered region at the middle portion, as predicted by program PONDR, indicating its potential for phase separation (Figure 3A; Romero et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an inference from the PONDR prediction and knowledge about phase separation.

claim: Both CAMSAP2-FL and GFP-CAMSAP2-FL formed droplets.
source: We thus investigated the droplet formation of CAMSAP2 in the polymerization PEM buffer, finding that both CAMSAP2-FL and GFP-CAMSAP2-FL formed droplets (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 10 nM GFP-CAMSAP2-FL could form the droplet under the salt concentration of less than 400 mM.
source: By examining a series of different GFP-CAMSAP2-FL and salt concentrations, we found that 10 nM GFP-CAMSAP2-FL, which approximates a physiological concentration, could form the droplet under the salt concentration of less than 400 mM, which is similar to TPX2 (King and Petry, 2020; Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by the phase diagram data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: 10 nM GFP-CAMSAP2-FL approximates a physiological concentration.
source: By examining a series of different GFP-CAMSAP2-FL and salt concentrations, we found that 10 nM GFP-CAMSAP2-FL, which approximates a physiological concentration, could form the droplet under the salt concentration of less than 400 mM, which is similar to TPX2 (King and Petry, 2020; Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a fact in the text.

claim: The droplet formation behavior of CAMSAP2 is similar to TPX2.
source: By examining a series of different GFP-CAMSAP2-FL and salt concentrations, we found that 10 nM GFP-CAMSAP2-FL, which approximates a physiological concentration, could form the droplet under the salt concentration of less than 400 mM, which is similar to TPX2 (King and Petry, 2020; Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is an inference from the data and comparison with cited literature.

claim: Two CAMSAP2 condensates fused and became a single large condensate when they came close to each other.
source: Once two CAMSAP2 condensates came close to each other, they fused and became a single large condensate (Figure 3E, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 3E and Video 1.

claim: Slow recovery of fluorescence was observed after photobleaching in a CAMSAP2 condensate.
source: We also observed the fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) in a CAMSAP2 condensate and found a slow recovery of the fluorescence (Figure 3F and G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by the FRAP data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: The CAMSAP2 condensates possess high viscosity.
source: These results suggest that the CAMSAP2 condensates possess high viscosity.
evidence: This is an inference from the fusion and FRAP data.

claim: Tubulin alone did not form any droplet in the physiological condition (PEM with 100 mM KCl).
source: In the physiological condition (PEM with 100 mM KCl), tubulin alone did not form any droplet but formed co-condensate only when mixed with GFP-CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Tubulin formed co-condensate only when mixed with GFP-CAMSAP2-FL in the physiological condition.
source: In the physiological condition (PEM with 100 mM KCl), tubulin alone did not form any droplet but formed co-condensate only when mixed with GFP-CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: CAMSAP2 forms condensates by phase separation mechanism, into which tubulins are recruited.
source: These findings suggest that CAMSAP2 forms condensates by phase separation mechanism, into which tubulins are recruited.
evidence: This is an inference from the phase separation and co-condensation data.

claim: Tubulin and GFP-CAMSAP2-FL co-condensed together when co-incubated at 37°C for 10 min in the physiological condition.
source: Ten micromolar tetramethylrhodamine (TMR)-labelled tubulin was co-incubated with 10–1000 nM full-length GFP-CAMSAP2-FL at 37°C for 10 min in the physiological condition (PEM with 100 mM KCl) (Figure 4A). These molecules co-condensed together, and importantly microtubules extended radially from the condensates (Figure 4B), as observed for the TPX2 aster-like structure (Roostalu et al., 2015; Schatz et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Microtubules extended radially from the CAMSAP2-tubulin condensates.
source: These molecules co-condensed together, and importantly microtubules extended radially from the condensates (Figure 4B), as observed for the TPX2 aster-like structure (Roostalu et al., 2015; Schatz et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The appearance of the CAMSAP2-tubulin structure was reminiscent of the centrosomal aster.
source: The appearance of this structure was reminiscent of the centrosomal aster; thus, we named it 'Cam2-aster'.
evidence: This is a qualitative observation and naming decision by the authors.

claim: Cam2-asters became detectable above 250 nM of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL.
source: Cam2-asters became detectable above 250 nM of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL, and the number of asters increased as the CAMSAP2 concentration raised from 250 to 1000 nM, consistent with our pelleting assay (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The number of asters increased as the CAMSAP2 concentration raised from 250 to 1000 nM.
source: Cam2-asters became detectable above 250 nM of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL, and the number of asters increased as the CAMSAP2 concentration raised from 250 to 1000 nM, consistent with our pelleting assay (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The CAMSAP2 concentration required for aster formation in vitro was higher than the putative physiological concentration of CAMSAP2 (tens of nanomolar).
source: The CAMSAP2 concentration required for aster formation in vitro was higher than the putative physiological concentration of CAMSAP2 (tens of nanomolar) (Wühr et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison between experimental conditions and cited physiological concentrations.

claim: CAMSAPs are concentrated at sub-cellular structures such as adherens junctions and cellular cortex through the interaction with some adapter proteins.
source: Previous reports have demonstrated that CAMSAPs are not only cytosolic but also concentrated at sub-cellular structures such as adherens junctions and cellular cortex through the interaction with some adapter proteins (Toya et al., 2016), and these CAMSAPs that are anchored to semi-solid structures sustained microtubule growth.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: CAMSAPs that are anchored to semi-solid structures sustained microtubule growth.
source: Previous reports have demonstrated that CAMSAPs are not only cytosolic but also concentrated at sub-cellular structures such as adherens junctions and cellular cortex through the interaction with some adapter proteins (Toya et al., 2016), and these CAMSAPs that are anchored to semi-solid structures sustained microtubule growth.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Local condensates of intrinsic CAMSAP2 were observed in HeLa cells before and during the polymerization of microtubules.
source: We also observed the local condensates of intrinsic CAMSAP2 in HeLa cells before and during the polymerization of microtubules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Tubulin was efficiently incorporated into the CAMSAP2 foci within 1 min.
source: Tubulin was efficiently incorporated into the CAMSAP2 foci within 1 min, although polymerization of microtubules was rarely observed (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Polymerization of microtubules was rarely observed when tubulin was added to fixed CAMSAP2 foci without free CAMSAP2 in solution.
source: Tubulin was efficiently incorporated into the CAMSAP2 foci within 1 min, although polymerization of microtubules was rarely observed (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by the TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Microtubule formation was induced from the CAMSAP2 foci when free GFP-CAMSAP2-FL was supplemented.
source: We thought that microtubule polymerization from CAMSAP2 foci might require free CAMSAP2 in solution, and we supplemented 10–1000 nM of free GFP-CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 4F). As a consequence, microtubule formation was induced from the CAMSAP2 foci.
evidence: This is supported by the TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 4G and H.

claim: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL at a concentration of 50 nM in solution was sufficient for efficient microtubule polymerization from the foci.
source: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL at a concentration of 50 nM in solution was sufficient for efficient microtubule polymerization from the foci, although higher concentrations of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL further increased the microtubule polymerization efficiency (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Higher concentrations of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL further increased the microtubule polymerization efficiency from fixed foci.
source: GFP-CAMSAP2-FL at a concentration of 50 nM in solution was sufficient for efficient microtubule polymerization from the foci, although higher concentrations of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL further increased the microtubule polymerization efficiency (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: When CAMSAP2 is physically fixed as observed in vivo, its concentration required for microtubule elongation could be reduced.
source: Thus, when CAMSAP2 is physically fixed as observed in vivo, its concentration required for microtubule elongation could be reduced.
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing efficient polymerization at 50 nM with fixed foci.

claim: Dynamic polymerization and depolymerization of microtubules occurred at CAMSAP2-containing foci with the association of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL.
source: We found that dynamic polymerization and depolymerization of microtubules occurred at CAMSAP2-containing foci with the association of GFP-CAMSAP2-FL (Figure 4I, Videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by the time-lapse TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 4I and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: The fixed foci of CAMSAP2 act as a core for microtubule polymerization, with free CAMSAP2 leading to the formation of microtubule asters.
source: These findings suggest that the fixed foci of CAMSAP2 act as a core for microtubule polymerization, with free CAMSAP2 leading to the formation of microtubule asters.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data with fixed foci.

claim: Spherical CAMSAP2 condensates were detected by negative stain electron microscopy.
source: We first observed condensates of CAMSAP2-FL by negative stain electron microscopy (EM) (Figure 5A). Consistent with light microscopy observations, the spherical CAMSAP2 condensates were detected.
evidence: This is supported by the EM data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: When 10 µM tubulin was incubated with 1 µM CAMSAP2-FL at 37°C for 30 min, microtubule bundles radiated extensively from each condensate.
source: When 10 µM tubulin was incubated with 1 µM CAMSAP2-FL at 37°C for 30 min, microtubule bundles radiated extensively from each condensate (Figure 5B), as found in the TIRF experiments (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by the negative stain EM data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Microtubule bundles from the neighbouring condensates further interacted, forming a dense microtubule meshwork.
